scope: Only the three-path doc_key child-FK index delta and its regression tests; no complete scale/task/release acceptance.

findings.detail: Adds one non-UNIQUE B-tree access path on existing chunk_symbol_identity(doc_key), both in fresh DDL and the existing current-schema writable-open maintenance branch. No table/column/constraint/trigger/serialization change or new data interpretation occurs. CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION remains 25 and all mismatch/rebuild branches remain unchanged. This does not require invalidating existing logical records.

The new production statement is only CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS. It changes SQLite physical schema/storage, as expected, but not user_version, row values, metadata epochs or an existing incarnation. The pre-existing read_generation::ensure call is untouched; its existing missing/corrupt-incarnation behavior is not newly introduced or claimed to be removed. Tests snapshot every SQL table, including metadata, before both writable opens.

DDL errors are mapped with db_err and propagated by ? before UpToDate. IndexDb::open_and_ensure_schema_inner propagates migration errors; only an explicit SchemaStatus::Mismatch enters destructive rebuild. No query_only disable, error swallowing, or fallback reset is added. The negative test checks refusal and unchanged rows; the independent SQL probe additionally proves the missing index remains absent after SQLITE_READONLY.

EXPLAIN executes DELETE on the real parent document_manifest filtered by chunk_id. The SQL contains no explicit child lookup; SQLite supplies the chunk_symbol_identity access from the doc_key foreign key. A dropped-index SCAN negative control, post-install SEARCH using the intended child index, and absence of child SCAN establish the access-path change. Actual deletion then removes only the intended child and checks foreign_key_check. These assertions inspect engine behavior, beyond merely matching DDL text.

The existing valid schema-25 database is opened twice and complete table snapshots stay identical. Fresh initialization requires the index. Existing v21/v24 fixtures and mismatch/rebuild contract remain in the same original regression target, which root reports and logs as 5/5 passing.

nonblocking_risks: First writable open of a large existing schema-25 DB pays one-time index-build CPU/IO/temp/WAL and writer-lock cost; concurrent openers may receive the existing busy/error result. This is an availability/capacity consideration, not a reason to relax correctness or retry/timeout receipts.

The maintenance batch contains two idempotent DDL statements without a new enclosing transaction. An earlier physical index may remain installed if a later statement fails; no logical rows are changed and the open still fails. Subsequent normal opens can retry existing idempotent maintenance.

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS does not repair an intentionally wrong same-name index definition. There is no such conflicting production index in the fixed base; arbitrary schema corruption is outside this delta.
suggested_followup_not_new_gate: Keep root 5/5 schema-guard results and the existing v21/v24/regression/source checks with the integrated fixed source.

During the already planned scale run, retain the one-time current-schema maintenance/open duration and any disk/busy failures. A focused concurrent-opener check is useful if that contention is observed; no new threshold is proposed.
